correctness.rationale: The source family is reconstructed exactly. The boundary derivative is purely imaginary and has a strictly decreasing scalar factor with one zero. At that zero, the radial imaginary part of the derivative factors exactly as a positive denominator times (sin t-cos t)(1+sin t+cos t)(1-r)^2/2, hence has the sign of 2s-1. The radial integral gives the same sign for Im(e^{-it}F), and the starlikeness quotient equals Y(t) Im(e^{-it}F)/|e^{-it}F|^2. Strict sign change therefore produces an interior point with negative real part for every s except 1/2.

value.rationale: The source introduces the family specifically as a transparent counterexample mechanism but proves failure on less than one fifth of the parameter interval. The accepted theorem shows that nonstarlikeness is generic across every unequal mixture and identifies an exact structural reason: a regular boundary derivative zero coupled to a radial sign factor proportional to 2s-1. This is a substantial classification of the fresh family, not a routine endpoint increment.
